mainTopic: God's laughter and daily schedule, converts in the future, and the value of Torah study
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why the nations' failure at the סוכה test is fair: even someone exempt because of suffering should not kick the סוכה. God then laughs at them, and רבי יצחק says God laughs only on that day. A second version attaches רבי יצחק's teaching to רבי יוסי's ברייתא about nations who attach themselves as converts in the future and then abandon their מצוות at the war of גוג ומגוג. The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק from רב's description of God's day, which includes playing with the לויתן, and answers that God plays 'with' His creations but laughs 'at' them only on that day. רב אחא adds that God has had no שחוק since the חורבן, and the גמרא searches for a פסוק to prove it. It then asks what God now does in the fourth part of the day and what He does at night. The amud closes with sayings on Torah study: warnings against idle talk, reward for learning at night, and people compared to fish. The last of these leads into ריש לקיש's teaching that in the future the sun will punish the wicked and heal the righteous, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Jews also sometimes suffer heat on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its answer: the test is fair, because Jews also sometimes face the summer heat lasting into סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because sometimes, for Jews too, the summer heat of תמוז stretches all the way to the festival, and sitting in the סוכה is painful for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started just before. Hot sun on סוכות is not an unfair trick on the nations, because Jews face the same situation in some years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that God brings the sun out on purpose to make the nations fail. The answer is that this kind of heat really happens to Jews too. So the nations are being tested under normal, real conditions.

keyTerms.meaning: The summer season (the hot season starting in the month of תמוז)

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָשְׁכָא לְהוּ תְּקוּפַת תַּמּוּז עַד חַגָּא,
phrases.english: that the summer season of Tammuz stretches for them until the festival,
and it is painful for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמָשְׁכָא לְהוּ תְּקוּפַת תַּמּוּז עַד חַגָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section, defending the fairness of the סוכה test.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the test reflects real conditions that apply to Jews too
steps.terutzMaskana: The heat on סוכות is a real situation Jews also face, so the test is fair.

steps.title: But someone suffering is exempt from the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבא rules that one who suffers is exempt from סוכה, so why blame the nations for leaving?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said: a person who is suffering is exempt from the סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the story. If heat makes the סוכה painful, leaving it is allowed, so why are the nations criticized?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule of מצטער says that real discomfort removes the obligation to sit in the סוכה. A Jew in the same heat would be allowed to leave. So leaving cannot be a failure.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say — introduces a challenge from a known ruling
One who is suffering or uncomfortable

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
one who is suffering is exempt from the sukka!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story by saying that leaving under such heat is permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the nations fail the test by leaving the סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If suffering exempts a person from סוכה, leaving because of heat is legitimate and cannot count as failing.

steps.title: Exempt, yes — but kicking is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: they may leave, but they should not kick the סוכה on the way out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that he is exempt, but should he kick it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The nations are not blamed for leaving. They are blamed for kicking the סוכה in scorn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption only lets you leave. It does not let you show contempt for the מצוה. The failure is in the attitude, not in the leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that, even if we admit that
Should they kick? — kicking in contempt

steps.whatToRemember: Being exempt from a מצוה lets you skip it, but never permits disrespecting it.

phrases.english: Granted that he is exempt,
but should they kick it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the סוכה. In the story just before, the nations kick their סוכה as they leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the fault from the action (leaving) to the manner (kicking)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nations were blamed simply for leaving the סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaving is allowed; kicking the סוכה in contempt is the real failure.

steps.title: God laughs at the nations
steps.stepSummary: The story continues: right away, God sits and laughs at the nations, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and laughs at them, as it says: 'He who sits in heaven laughs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to telling the story about the future. After the nations kick the סוכה, God laughs at them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for this is a פסוק in תהלים describing God laughing at the nations who rebel against Him. Their scornful act shows their true attitude, and God mocks them for it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said — introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: Immediately, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
sits and laughs at them,
as it is said: "He who sits in heaven laughs, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:4

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וּמְשַׂחֵק עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the side question, the גמרא resumes the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the nations kick the סוכה, God laughs at them, based on תהלים 2:4.

steps.title: God laughs only on that day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that God's laughter happens only on that one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: There is no laughter before the Holy One, Blessed be He, except on that day alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a comment on the פסוק of God laughing. He limits it to that single future day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think God often laughs at the wicked. רבי יצחק says this happens only on that special day of judgment of the nations.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׂחוֹק לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: There is no laughter before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
except on that day alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the פסוק quoted in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's laughter happens only on that one future day.

steps.title: Another version: רבי יוסי on the nations converting
steps.stepSummary: Some place רבי יצחק's teaching on a different ברייתא, where רבי יוסי says the nations will come and convert in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this statement of רבי יצחק on a different source, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says, in the future the nations of the world will come and convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version of where רבי יצחק's teaching belongs. It begins by quoting רבי יוסי's ברייתא about the nations converting in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version links רבי יצחק's teaching to a different future story. רבי יוסי says the nations will try to convert. The link to God's laughter comes later, so here the גמרא is only laying the groundwork.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (another version)

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק אַהָא,
phrases.english: There are those who teach this statement of Rabbi Yitzchak on this,
phrases.notes: They attach רבי יצחק's 'only that day' teaching to the ברייתא that comes next.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעָתִיד לָבֹא בָּאִין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּמִתְגַּיְּירִין.
phrases.english: In the future, the nations of the world will come and convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different setting for רבי יצחק's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: in the future, the nations will come and convert.

steps.title: But converts are not accepted in the days of משיח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי: a ברייתא says converts are not accepted in the days of the משיח, just as in the days of דוד and שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we accept them? But a ברייתא teaches: We do not accept converts in the days of the משיח, just as converts were not accepted in the days of דוד or in the days of שלמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי's statement. How can the nations convert in the future if another ברייתא says no converts are accepted then?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In times when the Jewish people are powerful and respected, like under דוד, שלמה and משיח, converts were not accepted. That ברייתא seems to contradict the idea that the nations will convert in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we accept? — a challenging question

phrases.english: And do we accept them?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּרִים לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: We do not accept converts in the days of the Messiah,
similarly, they did not accept converts

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּימֵי דָוִד וְלֹא בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה!
phrases.english: neither in the days of David nor in the days of Solomon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's statement from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that the nations will convert in the future
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says converts are not accepted in the days of the משיח, so the nations' conversion could not be valid.

steps.title: They become 'dragged-along' converts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: they are not formally accepted. They attach themselves on their own and put on תפילין, ציצית and מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they become self-made converts, who attach themselves, and they put תפילין on their heads, תפילין on their arms, ציצית on their clothes, and a מזוזה on their doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי יוסי does not mean they are formally accepted. He means they join on their own and start doing מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources are now true together. No court accepts them in the days of משיח, but the nations attach themselves on their own and act like Jews by doing these מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Dragged-along' converts — people who attach themselves on their own without being formally accepted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the nations become real, fully accepted גרים. The point is the opposite: they attach themselves without being formally accepted.

phrases.english: Rather, they become self-attached converts,
phrases.notes: Literally 'dragged' converts: they pull themselves in on their own, without a court accepting them.

phrases.english: and they put tefillin on their heads,
tefillin on their arms,
tzitzit on their garments, a mezuza on their doorways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by redefining what 'convert' means in רבי יוסי's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: self-attachment rather than formal acceptance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי meant the nations would be formally accepted as converts.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are not formally accepted. They attach themselves on their own and perform מצוות like תפילין, ציצית and מזוזה.

steps.title: The converts abandon their מצוות at the war of גוג ומגוג
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: when these self-attached converts see the war of גוג ומגוג, they learn it is against God and His משיח. Each one tears off his מצוה and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they see the war of גוג ומגוג, each convert asks the attackers why they came. They answer: to fight against God and His משיח, as the פסוק says. Then each convert tears off his מצוה and walks away, as the פסוק says, 'Let us tear apart their bands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing רבי יוסי's ברייתא and showing what happens to the people who attached themselves on their own. When the big war comes, they drop their מצוות and leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said these people were never formally accepted. They only attached themselves by wearing תפילין and ציצית and putting up a מזוזה. Here we see why that matters: their attachment is weak, and when the war of גוג ומגוג is against God Himself, they pull off those מצוות and walk away. Each part of the story is matched to a פסוק from the second chapter of תהלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The nations that will make a great war at the end of days
His anointed one, meaning God's משיח
Their bands or straps (from the פסוק)

phrases.english: Once they see the war of Gog and Magog,
phrases.notes: "They" are the converts from step 8 who attached themselves on their own.

phrases.english: he says to them: For what did you come?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: עַל ה׳ וְעַל מְשִׁיחוֹ,
phrases.english: They say to him: Against the Lord and against His Messiah,
as it is stated: "Why are the nations in an uproar
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:1

phrases.english: and the peoples mutter in vain, etc."
phrases.notes: The "etc." points to the next פסוק, 'against the Lord and against His anointed' (תהלים 2:2).

phrases.english: And each one tears off his מצוה and leaves,
phrases.notes: "His מצוה" means the תפילין, ציצית and מזוזה from step 8.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Let us tear apart their bands, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question in steps 7-8, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא of רבי יוסי and tells how the self-attached converts end up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the war of גוג ומגוג, the converts who attached themselves throw off their מצוות and leave.

steps.title: God laughs, and רבי יצחק limits it to that day
steps.stepSummary: God sits and laughs at them, as the פסוק says. רבי יצחק adds that God has laughter only on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: God sits and laughs, as the פסוק says, 'He who sits in heaven laughs.' רבי יצחק said: God has no laughter except on that one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the line about God laughing again, now as the end of רבי יוסי's ברייתא. Then it attaches רבי יצחק's teaching to it, as step 6 said some do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the wording of steps 4-5 on purpose. In this second version, רבי יצחק's statement belongs to רבי יוסי's ברייתא. רבי יצחק's claim that God laughs on only one day is what the גמרא is about to challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistake or a double copy. The גמרא is really repeating these words, because in this version רבי יצחק's teaching is placed here.

phrases.english: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and laughs,
as it is stated: "He who sits in heaven laughs, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:4

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׂחוֹק
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has no laughter
except on that day alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׂחוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes the ברייתא from step 9 with God's laughter, then attaches רבי יצחק's teaching, as described in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God laughs only on the day the nations rebel against Him and His משיח.

steps.title: Challenge: God plays with the לויתן every day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק from רב, who divides God's day into four parts. In the last part, God plays with the לויתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that true? רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the day has twelve hours. In the first three, God sits and learns תורה. In the second three, He judges the whole world. When He sees the world deserves to be destroyed, He gets up from the throne of judgment and sits on the throne of mercy. In the third three, He feeds the whole world, from the biggest animals to the tiniest eggs of lice. In the fourth three, He plays with the לויתן, as the פסוק says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק's claim that God laughs on only one day. It uses רב's teaching that God plays with the לויתן every single day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said God laughs only on that one day. רב's schedule describes God's ordinary day, every day, and includes three hours of playing with the לויתן. So it seems God laughs and plays daily, which contradicts רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: The giant sea creature God created

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
The day is twelve hours;
the first three:

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and studies Torah;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנִיּוֹת — יוֹשֵׁב וְדָן אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: the second three: He sits and judges the entire world;
once He sees that the world deserves destruction,
He rises from the throne of judgment
and sits on the throne of mercy;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלִישִׁיּוֹת — יוֹשֵׁב וְזָן אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: the third three: He sits and feeds the entire world,
from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice;
the fourth three: He sits and plays with the leviathan,
as it is stated: "This leviathan You formed to play with."
phrases.notes: תהלים 104:26. The question is left unsaid: so God plays every day, not only on that one day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks רבי יצחק's statement in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that God has laughter only on that one day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב says God plays with the לויתן for three hours every day, so God's laughter is not limited to one day.

steps.title: Playing with creations versus laughing at them
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that God plays with His creations every day. He laughs at His creations only on that one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: God plays together with His creations every day, like with the לויתן. But He laughs at His creations only on that one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing there are two different kinds of laughter. That way רב and רבי יצחק do not argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Playing with the לויתן is friendly play together with a creature, and that happens daily. Laughing at people who rebel against God is a different thing, a laughter of mockery. רבי יצחק meant only that second kind, which happens only on the day of גוג ומגוג.
steps.whatToRemember: God plays 'with' His creations every day, but laughs 'at' them only on the day the nations rebel at the war of גוג ומגוג. Both רב and רבי יצחק are correct. The next step adds that even the daily play stopped once the בית המקדש was destroyed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
With His creations He plays,
but at His creations He does not laugh
except on that day alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו מְשַׂחֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of step 11 and keeps רבי יצחק's statement standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: two different kinds of laughter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any laughter by God, even playing with the לויתן, would contradict רבי יצחק's 'only that day.'
steps.terutzMaskana: God plays with His creations every day. He laughs at His creations only on the day of the nations' rebellion, so רב and רבי יצחק agree.

steps.title: Since the בית המקדש was destroyed, God has no laughter
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא tells רב נחמן בר יצחק that from the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, God has no שחוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said to רב נחמן בר יצחק: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, there is no laughter for the Holy One, Blessed be He.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא adds a new idea to the discussion: ever since the חורבן, God has no שחוק at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said God plays with His creations every day, and step 11 said He plays with the לויתן. רב אחא says this playing stopped when the בית המקדש was destroyed. So the playing with the לויתן belongs to the time before the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The destruction of the Holy Temple
The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Acha said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed
there is no laughter for the Holy One, Blessed be He.
phrases.notes: So the play with the לויתן from step 11 was only before the חורבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the daily playing described in steps 11 and 12 by limiting it to the time before the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the destruction of the בית המקדש, God has no שחוק.

steps.title: What is the source that there is no laughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that God has no שחוק since the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that there is no laughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a פסוק that supports רב אחא's statement. This sets up a search through several possible sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idea about God's behavior needs a source in the פסוקים. The next steps will try out sources one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that there is no laughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב אחא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that God has no שחוק since the חורבן.

steps.title: First suggested source: God called for weeping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the source is the פסוק in ישעיהו where God called for weeping and mourning on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from what is written: "And the Lord God of hosts called on that day for weeping, for mourning, and for baldness, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out its first possible source: a פסוק where God calls for crying and mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if God called for mourning over the חורבן, there is no room for laughter. The word אילימא ('if you say') is a hint that this suggestion is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Baldness (tearing out hair as a sign of mourning)

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"And the Lord God of hosts called
on that day for weeping and for mourning
and for baldness, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That God has no שחוק since the חורבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 22:12, where God calls for weeping and mourning.

steps.title: Rejected: maybe only that one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first source, because the פסוק may mean mourning only on that one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that day only, and no more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first source. The פסוק says 'on that day', so it might only mean that one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא's claim is that laughter stopped forever after the חורבן. A פסוק about one day of mourning does not prove that the mourning never ends.

phrases.english: Perhaps that day and no more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק talks about 'that day', so it may only call for mourning on that one day, not forever.

steps.title: Second suggested source: If I forget you, Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a second source: the פסוק 'If I forget you, Jerusalem'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from what is written: "If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget; let my tongue cleave to my palate if I do not remember you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible source, the famous פסוק about never forgetting ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that God never forgets ירושלים in its ruined state, so He would not laugh.

phrases.english: Rather, from what is written:
"If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget

phrases.aramaic: תִּדְבַּק לְשׁוֹנִי לְחִכִּי אִם לֹא אֶזְכְּרֵכִי״,
phrases.english: let my tongue cleave to my palate if I do not remember you"
phrases.notes: תהלים 137:5–6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That God has no שחוק since the חורבן.

steps.title: Rejected: no forgetting does not mean no laughing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second source. Not forgetting ירושלים does not prove there is no laughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is forgetting that there is not, but laughter at least there is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second source as well. The פסוק only says ירושלים is not forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remembering something and laughing can both happen. So this פסוק proves there is no forgetting, but it does not prove there is no שחוק.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is forgetting that there is not,
but laughter, at least, there is!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 17.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק rules out forgetting, not laughter.

steps.title: The accepted source: I have long held My peace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the source 'I have long been silent, I keep still, I restrain Myself'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from this: "I have long been silent, I keep still, I restrain Myself, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting two sources, the גמרא gives the source it accepts, a פסוק in ישעיהו where God says He holds Himself back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק describes God as silent and holding Himself in for a long time. The גמרא accepts it as showing that God's joyful play has stopped, and it raises no rejection here.

keyTerms.meaning: I restrain Myself, hold Myself back

phrases.english: Rather, from this:
"I have long been silent, I keep still, I restrain Myself, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 42:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final, accepted source after two rejected ones.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ישעיהו 42:14, where God restrains Himself.
steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים were rejected: one may refer to a single day, and the other only rules out forgetting. The accepted source is 'הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי מֵעוֹלָם', which describes God holding Himself back.

steps.title: So what does God do in the fourth part of the day?
steps.stepSummary: If God no longer plays with the לויתן, what does He do in the fourth part of the day?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the fourth part of the day, what does He do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the play with the לויתן stopped, what fills that time slot now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב divided God's day into four parts, and the last part was for playing with the לויתן (step 11). Since that stopped after the חורבן, the fourth part needs a new activity.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourth part (the last of the day's four sections)

phrases.english: In the fourth part, what does He do?
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב's four parts of God's day in step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב's four-part day in light of רב אחא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What God does in the fourth part of the day now that He no longer plays with the לויתן.

steps.title: God teaches Torah to young schoolchildren
steps.stepSummary: In the fourth part of the day God teaches Torah to young schoolchildren, as a פסוק in ישעיהו shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sits and teaches Torah to young schoolchildren, as it says: "Whom will He teach knowledge, and whom will He make understand a message? Those weaned from milk, taken from the breasts." To whom does He teach knowledge and make understand a message? To those just weaned from milk and taken from the breasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that God now spends the fourth part of the day teaching Torah to little children. It brings a פסוק to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as a question followed by its answer: 'Whom does He teach?' Answer: 'those just weaned', meaning very young children. So the time that used to be for play is now used for teaching Torah to children.

keyTerms.meaning: Those just weaned from milk (very young children)

phrases.english: He sits and teaches
young schoolchildren Torah,
as it is said:
"Whom will He teach knowledge
and whom will He make understand a message?
Those weaned from milk, taken from the breasts."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 28:9

phrases.english: To whom does He teach knowledge
and to whom does He make understand a message?
To those weaned from milk and to those taken from the breasts.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹשֵׁב וּמְלַמֵּד תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the fourth part of the day, God teaches Torah to young schoolchildren (ישעיהו 28:9).

steps.title: Who taught the children before the destruction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught the young children before the חורבן, when God was playing with the לויתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And originally, who used to teach them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. Before the חורבן the fourth part of the day was used for play, so who was teaching the children then?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If God only began teaching the children after the חורבן, the גמרא wants to know who did it before. This sets up the final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Originally, at first (here: before the חורבן)

phrases.english: And originally, who used to teach them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a follow-up question on the answer of step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who taught the schoolchildren before the חורבן.

steps.title: Two answers: מטטרון, or God did both
steps.stepSummary: Either the angel מטטרון taught them, or God both played with the לויתן and taught the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: מטטרון. And if you want, say: He did both this and that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible answers. Either an angel named מטטרון taught the children, or God did both activities in the fourth part of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first answer, God's teaching of the children is new since the חורבן. According to the second, God always taught them, and the only change after the חורבן is that the play with the לויתן stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)

steps.whatToRemember: Since the חורבן, God no longer has שחוק. In the fourth part of the day He teaches Torah to young children. Before the חורבן, either מטטרון taught them, or God did both: He played with the לויתן and also taught them.

phrases.english: If you want, say: Metatron,
and if you want, say: He did this and that.
phrases.notes: God did both: He played with the לויתן and taught the children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with two possible answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the angel מטטרון taught the children before the חורבן, or God did both: He played with the לויתן and taught the children.

steps.title: What does God do at night?
steps.stepSummary: Having laid out God's activities during the day, the גמרא asks what He does during the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at night, what does He do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: we know what God does during the day, but what does He do at night? This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps divided God's day into parts. This question extends that picture to the night hours, which were not yet covered.

phrases.english: And at night, what does He do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from God's daytime activities to the night.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What God does during the night hours.

steps.title: First answer: the night is like the day
steps.stepSummary: One answer: at night God does the same things He does during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: the same as in the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first possible answer: God's night is just like His day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the simplest answer. Nothing new happens at night; God keeps doing the same activities that were listed for the daytime.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say; introduces one possible answer

phrases.english: If you want, say: similar to the day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At night God does the same things He does by day.

steps.title: Second answer: God rides through 18,000 worlds
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: God rides on a light כרוב and travels through eighteen thousand worlds, learned from a פסוק in תהלים read in a new way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: He rides on His light כרוב and flies through eighteen thousand worlds, as it says: 'The chariots of God are twenty thousand, thousands of שנאן.' Don't read 'שנאן' but 'שאינן' (that are not).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer: at night God travels through eighteen thousand worlds. It proves the number from a פסוק by reading one word differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God's chariots are 'twenty thousand.' By reading 'שנאן' as 'שאינן' ('which are not'), it means 'twenty thousand minus thousands that are not there.' The smallest amount of 'thousands' is two thousand, so 20,000 minus 2,000 leaves 18,000.

keyTerms.meaning: don't read it as ... but as ...; reading a word in a new way to learn something

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the text of the פסוק is wrong. The גמרא keeps the written פסוק and adds a second meaning by reading a word differently.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רוֹכֵב עַל כְּרוּב קַל שֶׁלּוֹ
phrases.english: And if you want, say: He rides on His light כרוב
and flies through eighteen thousand worlds,
as it says: 'The chariots of God are twenty thousand, thousands of שנאן,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:18. 'רִבֹּתַיִם' means two ten-thousands, so twenty thousand.

phrases.english: don't read it 'שנאן' but 'שאינן' (that are not).
phrases.notes: So: twenty thousand, minus 'thousands' that are not there. The fewest thousands is two thousand, which leaves eighteen thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רוֹכֵב עַל כְּרוּב קַל שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At night God rides a light כרוב through 18,000 worlds.

steps.title: Third answer: God listens to the angels' song
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: at night God sits and listens to the songs of the חיות, based on a פסוק that speaks of a song in the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: He sits and listens to song from the mouths of the חיות, as it says: 'By day God commands His kindness, and at night His song is with me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer: at night God listens to the songs of the heavenly creatures, and it brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק contrasts day and night: day is for 'kindness' and night is for 'song.' The גמרא reads 'song at night' as the angels singing to God at night.

keyTerms.meaning: heavenly creatures, a type of angel

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: יוֹשֵׁב וְשׁוֹמֵעַ שִׁירָה מִפִּי חַיּוֹת,
phrases.english: And if you want, say: He sits and listens to song from the mouths of the חיות,
as it says: 'By day God will command His kindness,
phrases.notes: תהלים 42:9

phrases.english: and at night His song is with me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: יוֹשֵׁב וְשׁוֹמֵעַ שִׁירָה מִפִּי חַיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third possible answer to the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At night God listens to the song of the חיות.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to 'what does God do at night': (1) the same as by day, (2) He travels through 18,000 worlds, (3) He listens to the angels' song.

steps.title: Stopping Torah for idle talk
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that someone who stops learning Torah to chat about ordinary things is punished with burning broom-tree coals, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: Anyone who stops learning Torah and busies himself with idle talk is fed coals of the broom tree, as it says: 'They pluck salt-wort by the bushes, and the roots of the broom are their food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic about Torah study, with a warning from רבי לוי against interrupting Torah for idle chatter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a wordplay: the פסוק says 'עלי שיח' (by the bushes), and 'שיח' also sounds like 'שיחה', talk. The same פסוק mentions 'roots of the broom' as food, so idle talk is linked to eating broom-tree coals.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is often quoted as a reason to avoid stopping in the middle of Torah learning for idle conversation.

phrases.english: רבי לוי said:
Anyone who stops from words of Torah
and busies himself with idle talk
is fed coals of the broom tree,
as it says: 'They pluck salt-wort by the bushes,
phrases.notes: איוב 30:4. 'שיח' (bush) sounds like 'שיחה' (talk); that's the link.

phrases.english: and the roots of the broom are their food.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: כׇּל הַפּוֹסֵק מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from God's schedule to sayings about Torah study.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Interrupting Torah for idle talk brings a punishment of broom-tree coals.

steps.title: Learning at night brings kindness by day
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that whoever learns Torah at night receives a 'thread of kindness' from God during the day, explaining the same פסוק from תהלים as cause and effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who learns Torah at night, God draws a thread of kindness over him by day, as it says: 'By day God will command His kindness, and at night His song is with me.' Why does God command His kindness by day? Because at night His song (Torah) is with me.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש praises learning at night and shows from a פסוק that it earns God's kindness in the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק used in step 27 is now read as cause and effect. The 'song at night' is Torah learning, and the 'kindness by day' is the reward. The last line spells this out: the kindness comes because of the night learning.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is busy learning Torah
a thread of kindness, God's special grace over a person

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק as in step 27, but there 'song' meant the angels' song to God. Here 'song' means a person's Torah learning at night.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
Anyone who learns Torah at night,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, draws over him
a thread of kindness by day,
as it says: 'By day God will command His kindness,
and at night His song is with me.'
Why does 'By day God command His kindness'?
Because at night His song is with me.
phrases.notes: 'His song' here means Torah, which the person learns at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי לוי's warning, ריש לקיש gives a positive reward for Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning Torah at night earns a thread of God's kindness during the day.

steps.title: Another version: this world is night, the next world is day
steps.stepSummary: Some report ריש לקיש's teaching differently: learning Torah in this world (like night) earns kindness in the next world (like day).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say ריש לקיש said: Anyone who learns Torah in this world, which is like night, God draws a thread of kindness over him in the World-to-Come, which is like day, as it says: 'By day God will command His kindness...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of ריש לקיש's teaching, using the same פסוק but with a different meaning of 'night' and 'day'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 'night' and 'day' are real hours. Here they are symbols: this world is dark like night, and the next world is bright like day. The reward moves from tomorrow to the World-to-Come.

phrases.english: Some say: ריש לקיש said:
Anyone who learns Torah
in this world, which is like night,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹשֵׁךְ עָלָיו חוּט שֶׁל חֶסֶד
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, draws a thread of kindness over him
in the World-to-Come, which is like day,
as it says: 'By day God will command His kindness, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same teaching of ריש לקיש from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning Torah in this world earns kindness in the World-to-Come.

steps.title: People are like fish: without Torah they die
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains a פסוק in חבקוק comparing people to fish: just as fish die on dry land, people die when they leave Torah and מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What does it mean, 'You make man like the fish of the sea, like creeping things with no ruler over them'? Why are people compared to fish of the sea? To teach you: just as fish die right away once they come up on dry land, so too people die right away once they leave Torah and מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about Torah, explaining a פסוק that compares people to fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is the fish's natural home, and without it they cannot live. Torah and מצוות are a person's 'water'; leaving them is like a fish leaving the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: what does the verse mean?; introduces an explanation of a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known picture of Torah as the life-source of the Jewish people, just as water is for fish.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
What is meant by what is written:
'You make man like the fish of the sea,
phrases.notes: חבקוק 1:14

phrases.english: like creeping things that have no ruler over them'?

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם כִּדְגֵי הַיָּם?
phrases.english: Why are people compared to fish of the sea?
To tell you:
Just as fish in the sea,
once they come up on dry land, die right away,
so too people,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁפּוֹרְשִׁין מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמִן הַמִּצְוֹת
phrases.english: once they leave words of Torah and the מצוות,
die right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of how important Torah study is, with a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who leave Torah and מצוות are like fish out of water: they die right away.

steps.title: Another lesson: like fish under a hot sun
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation of the fish comparison: just as fish die when the sun beats down on them, so do people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: just as fish in the sea die right away once the sun beats down on them, so too people die right away once the sun beats down on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different lesson from the same comparison of people to fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation is not about Torah but about being exposed to harsh heat. Both fish and people are fragile and can die quickly when the sun burns too strongly on them.

keyTerms.meaning: the sun beats down hot on them

phrases.english: Another explanation:
Just as fish in the sea,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁקָּדְרָה עֲלֵיהֶם חַמָּה מִיָּד מֵתִים,
phrases.english: once the sun beats down hot on them, die right away,
so too people,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁקָּדְרָה עֲלֵיהֶם חַמָּה מִיָּד מֵתִים.
phrases.english: once the sun beats down hot on them, die right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second explanation of the same comparison from step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People, like fish, die quickly when the sun beats down on them.
steps.whatToRemember: The fish comparison gets two lessons: (1) people without Torah and מצוות are like fish out of water; (2) people, like fish, can die from the sun's heat.

steps.title: Two possible worlds for the sun's harm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the sun's deadly heat from step 32 could mean this world or the World-to-Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this is about this world. And if you want, say it is about the World-to-Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next two steps. It names two ways to read 'the sun beats down on them' and will explain each one right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 did not say when the sun kills people. This line offers two options and does not choose between them. Each option will then get its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces one of several possible answers)

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is in this world,
phrases.notes: "It" means the sun beating down and killing people, from the fish comparison just before.

phrases.english: and if you wish, say it is in the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies when the sun-harm described in step 32 takes place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun's deadly heat can be read as happening either in this world or in the World-to-Come.

steps.title: This world: heat and cold are harms a person must avoid
steps.stepSummary: The 'this world' reading follows רבי חנינא. Everything comes from Heaven except harms from cold and heat, which a person must guard against himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about this world, that fits רבי חנינא. He said: everything is in Heaven's hands except cold and heat, as the פסוק says, 'Cold and heat are on the crooked path; whoever guards his soul will stay far from them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the first option with a teaching of רבי חנינא. In this world, a person can be harmed by natural dangers like cold and heat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא says most things are decided by Heaven, but harms from cold and heat are up to the person to avoid. The פסוק tells a person who guards his soul to keep away from them. So in this world, someone can die from exposure to the sun's heat, just like a fish on land.

keyTerms.meaning: In the hands of Heaven, decided by God
Here, sickness that comes from heat (רש״י)
One who guards his soul (protects himself)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא is not saying God has no control over cold. He means that guarding against these harms is the person's own job.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is in this world,
following רבי חנינא,
as רבי חנינא said:
Everything is in the hands of Heaven
except for cold and heat,
as it says:
"Cold and heat are on the crooked path;
phrases.notes: משלי 22:5. In משלי, פחים can mean snares, but רש״י explains it here as sickness that comes from heat, which is the point the גמרא needs.

phrases.english: whoever guards his soul will stay far from them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — כִּדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first option offered in step 33.
steps.raayaObject: That the sun can harm people in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's teaching that cold and heat are not in Heaven's hands, based on משלי 22:5.

steps.title: World-to-Come: the sun will judge the wicked and heal the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The 'World-to-Come' reading follows ריש לקיש. There will be no separate גיהנם; God will bring out the sun, which punishes the wicked and heals the righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about the World-to-Come, that fits ריש לקיש. He said: there is no גיהנם in the future. Instead, the הקדוש ברוך הוא will take the sun out of its sheath and it will burn hot. The wicked will be judged by it, and the righteous will be healed by it. The wicked will be judged...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second option with a teaching of ריש לקיש. In the future, the sun itself will be the punishment for the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says the future punishment is not a separate place called גיהנם. It is the sun's heat, released from its covering. The same heat has two effects: it punishes the wicked and heals the righteous. That is how people 'die' from the sun like fish.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place of punishment for the wicked

steps.whatToRemember: The sun that harms people can be read two ways: as a natural danger in this world (רבי חנינא), or as the punishment of the wicked in the World-to-Come (ריש לקיש), where the same sun heals the righteous.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is in the World-to-Come,
following רבי שמעון בן לקיש,
as רבי שמעון בן לקיש said:
There is no גיהנם in the future,
rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
takes the sun out of its sheath,
and it burns hot,
the wicked are judged by it,
and the righteous are healed by it.
The wicked are judged...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא — כִּדְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second option from step 33, as an alternative to step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That the sun will harm the wicked in the World-to-Come.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's teaching that in the future the sun will replace גיהנם.
